Right: the same triangle with no weights, so is_weighted() returns False." width="100%"} Returns whether this graph supports edge weights. This property is set when the graph is created and cannot be changed afterward. Weighted graphs can store numeric weights on edges, which are used in algorithms like shortest path, minimum spanning tree, etc. In weighted graphs: - each edge can have an associated numeric weight - weights represent costs, distances, capacities, etc. - algorithms consider weights when computing paths and metrics In unweighted graphs: - all edges are treated equally (implicit weight of `1`) - weights are ignored or unavailable - algorithms use hop count instead of weight sum ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph supports weights, `False` otherwise. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~is_directed`) : Whether the graph's edges have a direction. [](`~shortest_path`) : Find the shortest path, by weight or by hops. [](`~set_edge_attrs`) : Store values on edges. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A third item in each edge tuple is a weight: ::: {#e1e7cfa0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec ( ec.Graph.from_edges([("A", "B", 2.5)]).is_weighted(), ec.Graph.from_edges([("A", "B")]).is_weighted(), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: ::: ### Kilometers or roads The roads between twelve towns are weighted by their length in kilometers. Because the graph is weighted, `shortest_path()` adds up kilometers. With `weighted=False` it counts roads instead, and the two give different routes from Elmwick to Kestrel Bay: ::: {#afacbd08 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} towns = ec.towns() by_km = towns.shortest_path("Elmwick", "Kestrel Bay", return_list=True) by_roads = towns.shortest_path( "Elmwick", "Kestrel Bay", return_list=True, weighted=False ) by_km = [towns.get_label_from_id(n) for n in by_km] by_roads = [towns.get_label_from_id(n) for n in by_roads] towns.is_weighted(), by_km, by_roads ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (True, ['Elmwick', 'Calder', 'Halston', 'Kestrel Bay'], ['Elmwick', 'Greyford', 'Kestrel Bay']) ``` ::: ::: The shortest drive, 99 km over three roads, is on the left. The route with the fewest roads, on the right, is 101 km: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#9dc3a4a7 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} towns.plot( layout="pos", highlight=by_km, highlight_edges=list(zip(by_km, by_km[1:])), edge_label_by="km", label_by="label", width=360, height=360, legend=False, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
